sheikh-ahmad-nobleman-of-siam.name: Sheikh Ahmad Qomi
sheikh-ahmad-nobleman-of-siam.summary: A Persian-born merchant who settled in Thailand's Ayutthaya Kingdom in the early 17th century, rose to a powerful court office, and is regarded as the ancestor of the influential Bunnag family.

ayutthaya-kingdom.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
ayutthaya-kingdom.summary: A Thai kingdom centered on the city of Ayutthaya from 1351 to 1767, a major hub of international trade considered a precursor of modern Thailand.

massaman-curry.name: Massaman curry
massaman-curry.summary: A rich, mildly spicy Thai curry blending Persian, Indian, and Malay spices with Thai ingredients, typically made with chicken, potatoes, and peanuts in coconut milk.

kuku-food.name: Kuku
kuku-food.summary: Iranian dish of whipped eggs with other ingredients folded in, similar to a frittata or open-faced omelette but with less egg and a shorter cooking time.

gilan-province.name: Gilan province
gilan-province.summary: A province in northwestern Iran along the Caspian Sea, whose capital is the city of Rasht.

khollar.name: Khollar
khollar.summary: Village in Sepidan County, Fars province, Iran, with 281 people at the 2006 census. It was once home to an important centre of wine production.

kateh.name: Kateh
kateh.summary: A simple, sticky Iranian rice dish from the Caspian region, cooked faster than polo-style rice and often called Iran's 'everyday rice.'

lavash.name: Lavash
lavash.summary: A thin flatbread baked in a tandoor or on a griddle, a staple food in Armenia, eastern Georgia and parts of Iran.

qom.name: Qom
qom.summary: Holy city in Shia Islam in Iran, home to the Fatima Masumeh Shrine and the world's largest center of Shia Islamic scholarship, visited by about 20 million pilgrims a year.

mazandaran-province.name: Mazandaran
mazandaran-province.summary: An Iranian province on the southern Caspian coast, spanning forests, plains and the Alborz mountains including Mount Damavand, known for agriculture, fish farming and tourism.

gorgan.name: Gorgan
gorgan.summary: City in northern Iran near the Caspian Sea, capital of Golestan province, historically also known as Astarabad.

mespilus-germanica.name: Medlar
mespilus-germanica.summary: Large shrub or small tree in the rose family, cultivated since Roman times. Its fruit is usually available in winter and eaten when bletted, raw or cooked.

nowruz.name: Nowruz
nowruz.summary: The Iranian New Year, marking the spring equinox and rooted in Zoroastrianism, celebrated for over 3,000 years across West and Central Asia, the Caucasus, and South Asia.

hasht-behesht-palace-tabriz.name: Hasht Behesht Palace (Tabriz)
hasht-behesht-palace-tabriz.summary: A palace in Tabriz begun by Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan and completed around 1483–1486 by his son, described by a Venetian visitor as an octagonal, domed building with 32 chambers.

tabriz.name: Tabriz
tabriz.summary: A city in northwestern Iran and capital of East Azerbaijan province, historically also known as Tauris, noted today for its handicrafts and carpet weaving.

capture-of-tabriz-1514.name: Capture of Tabriz
capture-of-tabriz-1514.summary: The Ottoman entry into the Safavid capital Tabriz in September 1514, following their victory over Shah Ismail's army at the Battle of Chaldiran weeks earlier.

isfahan.name: Isfahan
isfahan.summary: City in central Iran that flourished from the 9th to 18th centuries and became the Safavid capital under Abbas the Great, renowned for its Persian-Muslim architecture.

hasht-behesht.name: Hasht Behesht
hasht-behesht.summary: A 17th-century pavilion in Isfahan, Iran, built for Safavid shah Suleiman I, which became an influential architectural model called the "Hasht Bihisht" style.

uzun-hasan.name: Uzun Hasan
uzun-hasan.summary: The strongest ruler of the Turkoman Aq Qoyunlu state (r. 1452–1478), who defeated rival powers to build an empire spanning Iran, Iraq, and Anatolia.

matrak-nasuh.name: Matrakçı Nasuh
matrak-nasuh.summary: A 16th-century Ottoman Bosnian polymath — statesman, mathematician, historian, geographer, cartographer, and swordmaster — who invented the combat sport Matrak and taught at the Enderun School in Constantinople.

jafar-pasha.name: Jafar Pasha
jafar-pasha.summary: Ottoman governor of Tabriz after its capture in 1585, a European convert to Islam ('neo-Muslim') in Ottoman service; the city stayed under Ottoman rule until 1603.

zamburak-iran.name: Zamburak
zamburak-iran.summary: A small cannon mounted on a camel and fired by its rider, the zamburakchi, meaning "little wasp" in Persian; used in the Iranian army from the 17th to early 20th century.

hormuz-island.name: Hormuz Island
hormuz-island.summary: An Iranian island in the Persian Gulf, occupied by the Portuguese from 1515 until the Safavids conquered it with English help in 1622.

nader-shah.name: Nader Shah
nader-shah.summary: Founder of Iran's Afsharid dynasty, ruling as shah from 1736 until his assassination in 1747; his campaigns built an empire stretching from India to the Caucasus.

battle-of-karnal.name: Battle of Karnal
battle-of-karnal.summary: 1739 battle in which Nader Shah's forces crushed the Mughal army in three hours, opening the way to the sack of Delhi and critically weakening the Mughal Empire.

muhammad-shah.name: Muhammad Shah
muhammad-shah.summary: Thirteenth Mughal emperor, reigning 1719 to 1748, whose rule saw the empire's rapid decline, worsened by Nader Shah's invasion and sacking of Delhi in 1739.

agha-mohammad-khan-qajar.name: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar
agha-mohammad-khan-qajar.summary: Founder of Iran's Qajar dynasty, ruling as Shah from 1789 to 1797; he reunified the country, made Tehran its capital, and campaigned to reassert Iranian rule over Georgia.

treaty-of-georgievsk.name: Treaty of Georgievsk
treaty-of-georgievsk.summary: A 1783 treaty making eastern Georgia a Russian protectorate under the Bagrationi dynasty; Russia later scrapped it in 1801, annexing Georgian lands directly and deposing the monarchy.

battle-of-krtsanisi.name: Battle of Krtsanisi
battle-of-krtsanisi.summary: 1795 battle in which Qajar Iran crushed Georgian forces near Tbilisi, leading to the city's destruction and Georgia's temporary reabsorption into the Iranian empire.

russo-persian-wars.name: Russo-Persian Wars
russo-persian-wars.summary: A series of five conflicts between Russia and Persia from 1651 to 1828 over control of the Caucasus, ending with Persia ceding its Transcaucasian territories to Russia.

treaty-of-turkmenchay.name: Treaty of Turkmenchay
treaty-of-turkmenchay.summary: 1828 treaty ending the Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828, forcing Qajar Iran to cede the Erivan, Nakhchivan and Talysh khanates in the South Caucasus to Russia.

russo-persian-war-1826-1828.name: Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828
russo-persian-war-1826-1828.summary: The last major war between Russia and Qajar Iran over the South Caucasus, ending in 1828 with the Treaty of Turkmenchay, which stripped Iran of its remaining Caucasus territories.

kermanshah.name: Kermanshah
kermanshah.summary: A city in western Iran, about 525 km from Tehran, now the capital of Kermanshah province with a population of roughly one million.

hamadan.name: Hamadan
hamadan.summary: A mountainous city in western Iran, among the oldest Iranian cities, identified with the ancient Ecbatana and once capital of the Medes.

shirvan.name: Shirvan
shirvan.summary: A historical Iranian region in the eastern Caucasus, known from the pre-Islamic Sasanian era through the early Islamic period, today part of Azerbaijan between the Caspian Sea and the Kura River.

erivan-khanate.name: Erivan
erivan-khanate.summary: An 18th-century Iranian province, also called Erivan, centred on present-day central Armenia; it became a Russian-Iranian battleground before being ceded to Russia in 1828.

abbas-the-great.name: Abbas the Great
abbas-the-great.summary: Fifth Safavid shah of Iran, ruling 1588-1629 and widely considered the dynasty's greatest ruler, who brought the empire to its military, political and economic height.

nishapur.name: Nishapur
nishapur.summary: A city in northeastern Iran, founded in the 3rd century by Shapur I, later capital of the Tahirid dynasty and initial capital of the Seljuk Empire.

heraclius-ii-of-georgia.name: Heraclius II
heraclius-ii-of-georgia.summary: King of Kakheti from 1744 and of the united Kartli-Kakheti from 1762 to 1798, in eastern Georgia; he unified the region and placed it under Russian protection in 1783.

catherine-the-great.name: Catherine the Great
catherine-the-great.summary: Empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796, who seized power from her husband Peter III and oversaw an era of territorial expansion and Enlightenment reform.

shusha.name: Shusha
shusha.summary: City in the Karabakh mountains that became capital of the Karabakh Khanate founded by Panah Ali Khan in the 1750s, and later a cultural center of the South Caucasus.

allahverdi-khan.name: Allahverdi Khan
allahverdi-khan.summary: Safavid general and statesman of Georgian origin (c. 1560–1613) who rose from a military slave to one of the most powerful officials under Shah Abbas the Great.

safavid-dynasty.name: Safavid dynasty
safavid-dynasty.summary: Ruling dynasty of Safavid Iran from 1501 to 1736, of Kurdish origin based in Ardabil; Shah Ismail I made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion, a turning point in Islamic history.

shahnameh.name: Shahnameh
shahnameh.summary: An epic poem of about 50,000 couplets written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi between around 977 and 1010 CE, telling Iran's mythical and historical past up to the Muslim conquest. It is regarded as Iran's national epic.

tahmasp-i.name: Tahmasp I
tahmasp-i.summary: Second shah of Safavid Iran, ruling from 1524 to 1576, who fought long wars with the Ottomans and Uzbeks and was a noted patron of painters, calligraphers and poets.

indian-style-poetry.name: Sabk-i Hindi
indian-style-poetry.summary: A Persian poetry style associated with poets at Indian courts in the Mughal era, sometimes also called sabk-i Isfahani or sabk-i Safavi after similarly styled Safavid-court poets.

nizami-ganjavi.name: Nizami Ganjavi
nizami-ganjavi.summary: 12th-century Persian poet (c. 1141-1209), considered the greatest romantic epic poet in Persian literature, author of the Khamsa, which includes Layla and Majnun.

aqa-mirak.name: Aqa Mirak
aqa-mirak.summary: Persian illustrator and painter active from around 1520 until his death in Qazvin in 1576.

sad-dar.name: Sad-dar
sad-dar.summary: A Persian Zoroastrian text known as "Hundred Doors," made up of a hundred chapters of guidelines for Zoroastrians to follow.

thomas-hyde.name: Thomas Hyde
thomas-hyde.summary: English linguist and orientalist (1636–1703) whose 1700 work on ancient Persian religion was the first to use Arab and Persian sources to correct Greek and Roman accounts of Zoroastrianism.

parsadan-gorgijanidze.name: Parsadan Gorgijanidze
parsadan-gorgijanidze.summary: A Georgian official and historian who served the Safavid court in Isfahan, known for his chronicle The History of Georgia.

abraham-hyacinthe-anquetil-duperron.name: Anquetil-Duperron
abraham-hyacinthe-anquetil-duperron.summary: First professional French Indologist (1731–1805) who helped introduce Indian texts such as the Upanishads to the West through his translations.

vendidad.name: Vendidad
vendidad.summary: The only volume of the Sasanian Avesta still present in the extant Avesta collection, a Zoroastrian text likely preserved through its use in liturgy.

william-jones-philologist.name: Sir William Jones
william-jones-philologist.summary: British philologist, scholar and judge (1746–1794) who served on the Bengal court and studied ancient Indian history; among the earliest to argue the Indo-European languages were related, and founder of the Asiatic Society in Calcutta in 1784.

pahlavi-scripts.name: Pahlavi
pahlavi-scripts.summary: A written form of Middle Iranian languages derived from the Aramaic script, used for texts from regions such as Parthia and Persis.

gunpowder-empires.name: Gunpowder empires
gunpowder-empires.summary: A term for three early modern Muslim empires, the Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal, that used newly invented firearms to conquer vast territory between the mid-16th and early 18th centuries.

qajar-dynasty.name: Qajar dynasty
qajar-dynasty.summary: An Iranian ruling family that gained prominence in the 16th century and governed Iran from 1789 to 1925, ending when Reza Shah was declared the new shah.

fath-ali-shah-qajar.name: Fath-Ali Shah Qajar
fath-ali-shah-qajar.summary: Second Shah of Qajar Iran, reigning from 1797 to 1834, whose wars with Russia cost Iran its Caucasus territories, though he also centralized the state and revived Persian arts.

ismail-i.name: Ismail I
ismail-i.summary: Founder and first shah of Safavid Iran, ruling from 1501 to 1524, who unified Iran under native rule and made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion, before being defeated by the Ottomans at Chaldiran in 1514.

twelver-shi-ism.name: Twelver Shi'ism
twelver-shi-ism.summary: The largest branch of Shia Islam, holding that twelve divinely appointed Imams beginning with Ali succeeded the prophet Muhammad, with the twelfth expected to return as the Mahdi.

mirwais-hotak.name: Mirwais Hotak
mirwais-hotak.summary: Afghan ruler (c. 1673–1715) of the Hotak sub-tribe who founded the Hotak dynasty after declaring independence from Safavid Persia around Kandahar in 1709.

hotak-dynasty.name: Hotak Dynasty
hotak-dynasty.summary: An Afghan dynasty of Ghilji Pashtuns founded in 1709 by Mirwais Hotak after rebelling against the Safavids; it briefly ruled parts of Iran and Afghanistan before its defeat by Nader Shah in 1738.

mahmud-hotak.name: Mahmud Hotak
mahmud-hotak.summary: Ruler of the Hotak dynasty, known as "the Conqueror", who overthrew the Safavid dynasty to become king of Persia from 1722 until his death in 1725.

afsharid-dynasty.name: Afsharid dynasty
afsharid-dynasty.summary: An Iranian dynasty founded by Nader Shah, who ruled 1736 to 1747, drawn from the Turkoman Afshar tribe, governing Afsharid Iran.

zand-dynasty.name: Zand dynasty
zand-dynasty.summary: An Iranian dynasty founded by Karim Khan Zand of the Zand tribe of the Laks, who ruled Iran from 1751 to 1779.

durrani-empire.name: Durranis
durrani-empire.summary: The Durrani Empire, founded in 1747 by Ahmad Shah Durrani, ruled much of present-day Afghanistan, Pakistan and neighbouring regions and was among the era's most significant Islamic empires.

khanate-of-kalat.name: Khanate of Kalat
khanate-of-kalat.summary: A Brahui-ruled khanate centered on Kalat in modern Pakistan, formed in 1666 against Mughal expansion; at its height it stretched from Kerman to Sindh before becoming a princely state of Pakistan in 1948.

chinggisids.name: Chinggisids
chinggisids.summary: The descendants of Genghis Khan and his wife Börte, who by tradition were considered the only legitimate rulers of the Mongol Empire and its successor states, a rule that lasted until 1847.

alids.name: Alids
alids.summary: Descendants of Ali, cousin and son-in-law of the prophet Muhammad, split into Hasanid and Husaynid branches and revered across the Muslim world.

buyid-dynasty.name: Buyid dynasty
buyid-dynasty.summary: A Shia Muslim dynasty of Iranian Daylamite origin that ruled Iraq and central and southern Iran from 934 to 1062, reviving symbols of the Sasanian Empire.

ardabil.name: Ardabil
ardabil.summary: A city in northwestern Iran and capital of Ardabil province, long known for silk and carpet trade, once briefly the principal city of Azerbaijan, and home to the tomb of Safavid founder Ismail I.

qizilbash.name: Qizilbash
qizilbash.summary: Turkoman Shia militant groups active from the late 15th century in Iranian Azerbaijan, Anatolia and the Caucasus, who helped found Iran's Safavid dynasty.

peacock-throne.name: Peacock Throne
peacock-throne.summary: The bejeweled imperial throne of the Mughal emperors, commissioned by Shah Jahan in the early 1600s and named for its mounted peacock figures, until Nader Shah carried it off as a war trophy in 1739.

koh-i-noor.name: Koh-i-Noor
koh-i-noor.summary: One of the largest cut diamonds in the world at 105.6 carats, looted from Delhi's Peacock Throne by Nader Shah in the 1740s and later given to Queen Victoria in 1849.

karim-khan-zand.name: Karim Khan Zand
karim-khan-zand.summary: Founder of the Zand dynasty who ruled most of Iran from 1751 to 1779, bringing peace and prosperity after decades of war and restoring relations with Britain.

safi-ad-din-ardabili.name: Safi-ad-Din Ardabili
safi-ad-din-ardabili.summary: A Kurdish poet, mystic and Sufi master (1252/3-1334) who led the Sufi order later called the Safaviyya from 1301; ancestor of the Safavid dynasty that ruled Iran from 1501.

muhammad.name: Muhammad
muhammad.summary: The founder of Islam, born around 570 CE in Mecca, whom Muslims believe received revelations from God beginning around 610 as the final prophet.

george-xi.name: George XI
george-xi.summary: A Georgian monarch who ruled the Kingdom of Kartli as a Safavid Persian subject (1676-1688, 1703-1709) and later served as Safavid commander-in-chief in what is now Afghanistan, known in Iran as Gurgin Khan.

kaikhosro-of-kartli.name: Kaikhosro of Kartli
kaikhosro-of-kartli.summary: Titular king of Kartli in eastern Georgia from 1709 to 1711, who ruled in absentia while serving as a Persian commander-in-chief in what is now Afghanistan.

treaty-of-resht.name: Treaty of Resht
treaty-of-resht.summary: 1732 treaty between Russia and the Safavid Empire in which Russia gave up territory south of the Kura River taken by Peter I in the 1720s.

treaty-of-constantinople-1736.name: Treaty of Constantinople (1736)
treaty-of-constantinople-1736.summary: A 1736 treaty between the Ottoman Empire and Afsharid Iran that ended the Ottoman–Persian War of 1730 to 1735.

topal-osman-pasha.name: Topal Osman Pasha
topal-osman-pasha.summary: Ottoman military officer and administrator (1663–1733) who served as Grand Vizier and later led Ottoman troops against Nader Shah, dying in the Battle of Kirkuk.

battle-of-yeghev-rd.name: Battle of Yeghevārd
battle-of-yeghev-rd.summary: The final major battle of the 1730 to 1735 Ottoman-Persian War, in which an advance guard of Nader's army routed a much larger Ottoman force in the Caucasus, cementing his reputation as a military genius.

mulla-sadra.name: Mulla Sadra
mulla-sadra.summary: Iranian Islamic philosopher, theologian and mystic (c. 1571/2 – c. 1635/40) who led Iran's 17th-century cultural renaissance and is considered by some the most influential Muslim philosopher of the last four centuries.

oliver-leaman.name: Oliver Leaman
oliver-leaman.summary: American professor of philosophy (born 1950) specializing in Islamic, Jewish and Eastern philosophy, teaching at the University of Kentucky.

shihab-al-din-yahya-ibn-habash-suhraward.name: Suhrawardi
shihab-al-din-yahya-ibn-habash-suhraward.summary: A Persian philosopher (1154–1191) who founded the Illuminationist school of Iranian philosophy and was executed for heresy.
shihab-al-din-yahya-ibn-habash-suhraward.source_title: Shihab al-Din Yahya ibn Habash Suhrawardi

ibn-arabi.name: Ibn Arabi
ibn-arabi.summary: An Andalusian Sufi mystic, poet and philosopher (1165–1240) whose vast writings, especially on the 'unity of existence,' became a dominant framework across the Muslim world.

transcendent-theosophy.name: Transcendent Theosophy
transcendent-theosophy.summary: A doctrine developed by Persian philosopher Mulla Sadra, who died in 1635, one of the two main disciplines of Islamic philosophy still active today.

illuminationism.name: Illuminationism
illuminationism.summary: A mystical and philosophical school founded by 12th-century thinker Suhrawardi, blending Avicennan, Peripatetic and Neoplatonic ideas into a distinct strand of Islamic philosophy.

qazvin.name: Qazvin
qazvin.summary: A city in northwestern Iran that served as capital of the Safavid Empire from 1555 to 1598 and is known today as Iran's calligraphy capital.

mir-damad.name: Mir Damad
mir-damad.summary: Iranian Twelver Shia philosopher (c. 1561–1631/32) in the Peripatetic tradition of Avicenna, founder of the School of Isfahan and teacher of Mulla Sadra.

baha-al-din-al-amili.name: Baha al-Din al-Amili
baha-al-din-al-amili.summary: A Twelver Shia scholar and polymath at the Safavid court (1547–1621), closely tied to Shah Abbas the Great and credited with shaping Isfahan's urban design and architecture.

fars-province.name: Fars province
fars-province.summary: A province in southwestern Iran, historically known as Persis, whose capital is the city of Shiraz.

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras
pythagoras.summary: Ancient Greek philosopher and polymath (c. 570–495 BC) from Samos, founder of Pythagoreanism, later credited with the Pythagorean theorem and the doctrine of transmigration of souls.

avicenna.name: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
avicenna.summary: Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), known in the West as Avicenna, was a leading philosopher and physician of the Islamic Golden Age whose Canon of Medicine remained a standard European medical text until 1650.

the-book-of-healing.name: The Book of Healing
the-book-of-healing.summary: A four-part scientific and philosophical encyclopedia by Avicenna, written around 1014–1027, covering logic, natural science, mathematics and metaphysics, meant to "heal" ignorance of the soul rather than treat the body.

turco-persian-tradition.name: Turco-Persian tradition
turco-persian-tradition.summary: A composite culture arising in the 9th–10th centuries in Khorasan and Transoxiana, Persian in its lettered tradition, Turkic in its rulers, and Islamic in outlook; it later spread across South, Central and West Asia.

safavid-order.name: Safavid order
safavid-order.summary: A Sufi order founded in Ardabil, renamed the Safaviyya and led by Safi-ad-Din Ardabili from 1301 to 1334; its later leaders sought political power and founded the Safavid dynasty in 1501.

lar-iran.name: Lar
lar-iran.summary: City in Fars province, Iran, serving as capital of both Larestan County and its district.

larestan-county.name: Larestan County
larestan-county.summary: County in Fars province, Iran, whose capital is the city of Lar.

new-julfa.name: New Julfa
new-julfa.summary: The Armenian quarter of Isfahan, Iran, established in the early 17th century and named after the older city of Julfa; still one of the largest Armenian quarters in the world.

ibn-bazzaz.name: Ibn Bazzaz
ibn-bazzaz.summary: A 14th-century Persian author from a family of cloth sellers who wrote the Safvat as-safa, a hagiography of the Sufi founder of the Safavid order.
